notes: Company overview: mid-stage ecommerce platform with personalized product search + messaging. Heavy embeddings use for personalization and reranking; planning migration from managed API to Dedicated capacity to reduce per-token cost and gain predictable throughput.

Workload profile (from customer): steady-state 1,200 QPS for embedding lookup requests during sales windows; baseline 400 QPS for chat-based support flows; burst peaks up to 6,000 QPS during promotions (10-15 minute windows).
Token characteristics: embedding ops ~128 tokens per call (avg); chat generation median 90 tokens, 95th 420 tokens; token/sec per request varies — need to model tail impact.
Latency SLOs: customer target 95th latency < 250ms for embedding lookups; 95th token-latency for chat generation < 1s; cost sensitivity — wants to cap monthly inference spend while maintaining SLA.

Model preferences: open models (LLama-derivative and mixture-of-experts), experimenting with 8-bit/4-bit quantized variants for cost reduction. Wants automatic fallback to smaller model family when Dedicated capacity saturated.
Routing & availability: geo-aware routing (NA primary, EU for EU customers) and automated regional failover. Requires VPC peering and control-plane isolation for PII workloads.
Security: must pass enterprise security questionnaire; require SSO (SAML), KMS integration for keys, audit logs retention 1 year, and EU data residency for subset of traffic.

POC ask: 2-week POC with a capped commit for Reserved GPUs to validate throughput and latency targets. Interested in canonical Redwood Optimize suggestions (batching + cache) before sizing finalization.
Quote from Priya (platform lead): "We need predictable tail latency during flash sales — occasional cost spikes are tolerated but not SLA breaches."
Internal AE notes: prioritize Dedicated GPU recommendation that balances A100-80GB vs H100 for quantized workloads; prepare conservative and aggressive sizing scenarios (steady vs peak).

Workshop deliverables expected by customer: GPU sizing table (GPU type, count, expected QPS per GPU, tokens/sec), latency heatmap across request sizes, recommended autoscale/burst runway and fallback model matrix, rough monthly cost estimate at steady and peak, SLA draft items (uptime, latency, credits).

workshop_notes: Pre-workshop data already received: 7 days of traffic traces (sampled), token histogram CSV, model config list (quantization variants), and current API latency percentiles.
Baseline assumptions for sizing exercise: 95th token-latency target for chat = 1s; embedding lookup 95th <= 250ms. Use sequence length distributions provided to simulate token/sec throughput.
Sizing scenarios to produce: (A) conservative steady-state (1,600 QPS embedding + 500 QPS chat) (B) expected average (3,000 total QPS) (C) peak flash sale (6,000 QPS for 12 minutes).
GPU options to evaluate: H100 80GB (higher single-request throughput, larger KV cache), A100-80GB (more cost-effective for quantized Llama), and mixed pool with smaller low-cost GPUs for fallback.
Autoscale policy draft: keep a warm pool sized for 1.5x steady-state; automatic burst to reserved burst capacity for up to 20 minutes; fallback to smaller model variants after 30s queue/backpressure.
SLA negotiation points to prepare: guaranteed throughput per-minute for committed GPUs, latency SLO with credits, maintenance windows, and clear definitions of force majeure for flash events.
